accepted.evidence: Turner 10452 explicitly lists European Romani ǰal 'goes' from yā́ti. The source specifically identifies Zargari džejipej 'to go' as an irregular infinitive from džā- (§3.17.3.2, p. 142), distinguishing this present stem from the gatá-derived irregular past linked in pass100. The infinitive formation is source morphology, not a separate etymon. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner 5055 explicitly lists European Romani čiv- 'to throw, put' in its section crossed with kṣipáti. The source prints Zargari čuv [čuw] 'Throw!' in §2.3.20 (p. 128), while giving final /v/ > [w]. The i/u vowel difference is retained as a local form, not explained by an invented sound rule. This short imperative is assigned to the attested Romani branch with Turner's crossing retained in the note, not to a bare kṣipáti node. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

held.reason: Turner 14048 gives European Romani asel 'laughs', and source p. 127 prints āssajipej 'to laugh'; the extra -aj- stem formation and whether it reflects a causative or local inflection remain unresolved.
The source prints the irregular past 'came' (p. 140), but the exact āv-/ay- branch and its relationship to the inherited present stem remain unresolved; do not transfer Turner's go etymon to it.
